systems.title: 5-Minute Grab-and-Go Bag
systems.description: A backpack near the exit for when you need to leave. This is the minimum critical layer, not the whole preparedness system.

systems.title: 15-Minute Ready Duffel
systems.description: 72-Hour Continuity Kit. A larger duffel for about 72 hours, adjusted for climate, travel, medical needs, children, and pets.

systems.title: 20-Minute Vehicle OR Suitcase Prep
systems.description: Choose a vehicle kit or an evacuation suitcase. These are two paths, not one combined chore.

systems.title: 60-Minute Home Resilience
systems.description: Sixty minutes for the highest-priority safety and continuity needs inside the home.

systems.title: Off-Grid Systems
systems.description: Stay capable when the grid is down. Low tech tools, sanitation, alternative cooking, and manual household systems for days without utilities.

systems.title: Water Purification
systems.description: Store, filter, and treat what you drink. Storage, filtration, purification, rotation, and emergency collection beyond the bottles in the pantry.

systems.title: Emergency Cooling / Heat
systems.description: Stay safe in extreme temperatures. Blackout cooling, shaded rooms, hydration, and safe warmth when HVAC is not an option.

systems.title: Home Battery & Solar
systems.description: Keep essential loads running. Plan battery capacity, solar input, safe charging, and which devices actually matter overnight.

systems.title: Long-Term Food
systems.description: A pantry built for weeks, not a weekend. Staples, rotation, preservation, and manual food prep for the stretch after the first few days.

systems.title: Medical Continuity & Accessibility
systems.description: Keep care going through a short disruption. This is planning, not medical advice.

systems.title: Sanitation & Contamination Control
systems.description: Toilets, handwashing, trash, and keeping clean water clean when utilities fail.

systems.title: Wildfire & Smoke
systems.description: Leave early when told. Protect breathing while you can still do it calmly.

systems.title: Flood & Flash Flood
systems.description: Water rises faster than it looks. Do not drive through it.

systems.title: Earthquake
systems.description: Protect yourself during shaking, then check the home before you use utilities.

systems.title: Tornado & Severe Wind
systems.description: Know the safest room before the warning.

systems.title: Hazardous Materials & Chemical Release
systems.description: If officials say shelter in place or evacuate, do that.

systems.title: Public Health
systems.description: Short-term illness and outbreak preparedness. Follow public-health instructions.

systems.title: Urban, Apartment & Shared Building
systems.description: Stairs, neighbors, limited storage, and a building plan.

systems.title: Children, Seniors, Pets & Caregivers
systems.description: Plans for the people and animals who depend on you. Supplies for the suitcase live on the suitcase path.

systems.title: Documents, Finances, Privacy & Recovery
systems.description: What you need to restart after a disruption. Keep account numbers and PINs off paper.

sections.title: Communication & Light
sections.intro: Keep these charged and next to the door.

sections.title: Identification & Money
sections.intro: One set per adult.

sections.title: Grab It
sections.intro: The bag should be accessible near the exit, not buried in a closet.

sections.title: Immediate Personal Needs
sections.intro: One set per person who needs them.

sections.title: Additional Grab-and-Go Items
sections.intro: Useful once the bag by the door is already packed.

sections.title: Water, Food & Protection
sections.intro: Kept for anything you add yourself. The primary water, light, and protection items are in the sections above.

sections.title: Documents
sections.intro: Store originals in a fireproof, waterproof safe. Carry copies in the bag.

sections.title: Clothing & Protection
sections.intro: Three days per person. Prioritize durable, quick-drying layers.

sections.title: Hygiene
sections.intro: Travel-sized items for three days per person.

sections.title: Medical
sections.intro: Customize to your household. Check expiration dates.

sections.title: Communication & Navigation
sections.intro: Stay informed when networks are strained.

sections.title: Food & Water
sections.intro: About three days of no-cook food. Cooking gear is in the next section.

sections.title: Cooking & Water
sections.intro: Outdoor cooking only. Never use a camp stove, grill, charcoal, or generator indoors or in an enclosed space.

sections.title: Emergency Protection
sections.intro: Protection for weather, smoke, and a night away from home.

sections.title: Vehicle Safety & Recovery
sections.intro: Keep a durable kit in the trunk. Review quarterly.

sections.title: Suitcase Prep
sections.intro: If you have about 20 minutes, pack continuity — not just survival.

sections.title: Fire, Smoke & Carbon Monoxide
sections.intro: Test alarms. Know two ways out.

sections.title: Utilities
sections.intro: Know the shutoffs before you need them. Follow utility guidance.

sections.title: Heat & Cooling
sections.intro: One room you can cool, and one room you can keep warm.

sections.title: Medication & Care Continuity
sections.intro: Follow your clinicians. This list does not replace their instructions.

sections.title: Wildfire & Smoke
sections.intro: Follow evacuation orders and local fire guidance first.

sections.title: Flood
sections.intro: Turn around. Do not walk or drive through floodwater.

sections.title: Shelter or Leave
sections.intro: Follow the alert. Do not go toward the source.
